clue.text: Fish, carp skinned for old cavalryman

parts.note: huss is a fishmonger's name for dogfish

indicators.note: with its skin removed, the word carp loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: An angler dresses a carp and serves it to a retired horse soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Hussars were light cavalry troopers in European armies, so a historic mounted soldier.

clue.text: Fish — stop to catch one before unhooking heads

indicators.note: the stopping word catches, i.e. holds inside, the other letters

parts.note: to halt is to stop
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the heads of the words before and unhooking are their first letters

explanation.surface: An angler pauses to land a fish before taking the hooks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' means the stop word holds the rest; 'heads' takes initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flatfish of northern seas, so an example of the general category.

clue.text: Small fish, rock

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
hake is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's label for a little fish and a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to rock something is to shake or jolt it back and forth.

clue.text: Dance laden with male trips

indicators.note: the letters stumble or trip over one another into a new order

explanation.surface: A dance is weighed down because a man keeps stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' looks like part of the dance floor scene but signals the anagram of LADEN MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtly German-style dance of the baroque period, and a suite movement named after it.

clue.text: A travesty, fishy fizzy drink?

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family, so a fishy word here
ade is a sweetened, often carbonated, fruit drink as in lemonade

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a fizzy drink that tastes of fish as a travesty.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a sham that mocks the real thing.

clue.text: Pair of fish for an apple

parts.note: the pair of fish starts with a cod, a common sea fish
ling is a long sea fish of the cod family, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: Two fish swapped for a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A codling is a variety of cooking apple, long and tapering.

clue.text: Equally prepared for benefit

parts.note: as, as in 'as tall as', expresses equality
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: Something equally ready to serve as a benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage or useful quality; a benefit to someone is an asset to them.

clue.text: Battle where a trap may be tried?

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals
a court is where a case may be tried

explanation.surface: A question about which battlefield saw a trap sprung.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as A GIN COURT: a court where a trap might stand trial, a whimsical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1415 English victory over the French under Henry V.

clue.text: Remarkably English, one side of literature?

parts.note: the verso is the left-hand page of a book

explanation.surface: A remark on how English one page of a book is.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase is an informal intensifier, meaning very or extremely.

clue.text: One's running — the pain from it?

definitions.meaning: a running ... is a basic sewing ...
a sharp side pain caused by running

explanation.surface: A jogger wonders whether the ache comes from the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a sewing loop (the running kind) and a sudden ache in the side during exercise.

clue.text: Given a flyer, teal fled in a panic carrying first of eggs

indicators.note: the scrambled letters carry, i.e. hold inside, the next letter
a panicked group of letters scatters into a new order
first of means only the opening letter of the word eggs is taken

explanation.surface: A duck takes flight in alarm, clutching an egg, after being handed a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a panic' rearranges TEAL FLED to LEAFLTED; 'carrying' takes E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle: to have had a printed handout delivered, as voters are.

clue.text: Harpoon small fish

parts.note: pike is a freshwater predator fish

explanation.surface: An order to spear a little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to spike is to impale on a sharp point, as a harpoon does.

clue.text: Ray gobbling river fish

indicators.note: the first word swallows the letter inside it

parts.note: a ray of light is a beam
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A ray, the flat fish, eats a river fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like the fish but means a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of the carp family, an example of the category.

clue.text: Embellish crypt with this series of art works

indicators.note: to embellish is to dress up and rework, here the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Instructions to decorate a church crypt with a set of paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-panel paintings, often altarpieces, so works of art arranged in panelled sets.

clue.text: Fish's gathered in, a little under a foot

indicators.note: the fish has gathered the next word into its middle

parts.note: tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish, once landed, measures just short of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten inches is two short of the twelve in a foot, as with a ruler.

clue.text: Old coin ending in circulation with European note in particular

indicators.note: the other letters go inside the word for particular

parts.note: nice can mean particular or precise, as in a nice distinction

indicators.note: the final letter of circulation

parts.note: to pen is to write, i.e. to note down

explanation.surface: A coin that has gone out of use, with a European note still in circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'particular' is used in its old sense of precise, as in a nice point. The answer is a pre-1971 British sum, nine old pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine pence was a British pre-decimal sum, and a silver coin of that value once circulated.

clue.text: Plastering material to see in face that's been knocked about

indicators.note: knocked about, i.e. turned round, so the whole is read backwards
the seeing word goes inside the face word

parts.note: mug is slang for face
to spy is to see

explanation.surface: Plaster is needed to fix a face that has taken a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked about' looks like an anagram signal but here means turned around: the container MUSPYG is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft mineral, calcium sulphate, which is heated to make plaster of Paris.

clue.text: A few lines, silver fish hooks and a perch to be gutted

indicators.note: the fish hooks the silver, holding it inside

parts.note: a parr is a young salmon
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: gutting the word perch leaves only its outside letters

explanation.surface: An angler's tale: a silvery fish hooked, and a perch to be cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: A parr is a young salmon; the fish hooking the silver gives PARAGR.
explanation.definitionFit: A block of text of a few sentences, the usual unit in prose writing.

clue.text: Communist sticks by workers, wiping brow

indicators.note: the brow is the top, so the first letter is wiped off

parts.note: men are workers, as in a firm's staff
gels means sets firm or sticks together

explanation.surface: A communist stands by the workers, mopping his forehead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiping brow' removes M from MEN, leaving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote the Communist Manifesto with Marx, so a founder of the movement.

clue.text: Fish, small fish

parts.note: a kipper is a split smoked herring

explanation.surface: A menu list of fish, then a smaller one.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipper is a name for the saury and some other fish, an example of the category.

clue.text: Score in second haul of fish about right

indicators.note: the catch goes around the letter

parts.note: a catch is a haul of fish

explanation.surface: A fishing crew scores on its second haul, just about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside CATCH. 'Score' is not twenty but a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to score a surface is to mark it with a line, to graze it.

clue.text: Haitian leader buried in revolution, cross beneath it, monolithic statue

indicators.note: in a down entry the cross sits below the rest
the letter is buried inside the turning word

parts.note: a spin is a revolution, a turn

indicators.note: the leader of the word Haitian is its first letter

parts.note: X is a cross

explanation.surface: A Haitian leader lies buried during a revolution, a cross and a stone statue above.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Sphinx of Giza is carved from a single mass of rock, a huge monolith.

clue.text: Male parent cracking and failing as a leader

parts.note: he is a male pronoun

indicators.note: the parent cracks into the other letters, sitting inside them
a failing word falls apart into a new order

parts.note: ma is mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A father is cracking up and failing in his role as head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male parent' looks like one idea, father, but splits in two. 'failing' rearranges 'and' to ADN, and 'cracking' gives ADMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief of a village or tribe, i.e. its head or chief.

clue.text: Sample fish, including last of blenny

indicators.note: the trout includes the letter inside it

parts.note: a trout is a fish

indicators.note: the last letter of blenny

explanation.surface: Taste a fish dish with a bit of blenny in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run lets one sample or test something before committing.

clue.text: Smothered in sauce, local appearing put out again

indicators.note: the pub is smothered, covered all round, by the sauce

parts.note: relish is a sauce or condiment
a local is a British pub near home

explanation.surface: A pub drowned in sauce makes a strange reappearance.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a book or article in print once more, i.e. to reissue it.

clue.text: Cold fish

definitions.meaning: a small silvery river fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Someone is described as an unfeeling person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold fish' reads as one insult, an unfriendly person, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: chilly and exposed, and a small freshwater fish.

clue.text: Obliged to leave, depart finally amid word of appreciation

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: the letter goes amid the word of thanks

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

indicators.note: the last letter of depart

explanation.surface: Someone has to leave and finally depart amid thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial contraction of 'got to', meaning must or having a duty.

clue.text: Supercharger cutting fish

indicators.note: cutting the word means docking its tail letter

parts.note: a turbot is a large flatfish

explanation.surface: A powerful engine part slicing through a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbocharger, an engine booster driven by exhaust gases, informally shortened.

clue.text: Cat attack not kicking off

indicators.note: the word does not start, losing its opening letter

parts.note: to pounce is to spring in attack

explanation.surface: A cat's attack fails to start.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called the ounce, a big cat of central Asia.

clue.text: Emin's back in seaside town, quiet retiring star!

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole is read in reverse
that letter goes inside the town's name

parts.note: Margate is a seaside resort in Kent

indicators.note: the back of the name Emin is its last letter

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: Artist Tracey Emin returns to her seaside home town, a quiet, retiring star.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin grew up in Margate, a Kent seaside resort. 'in' puts N inside it to make MARGATNE; add P and 'retiring' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star drawn in one continuous line, used as a symbol.

clue.text: Sci-fi fan runs after vacuous Kirk into wood

indicators.note: the letter comes after the rest
those letters go into the tree

parts.note: a tree is wood

indicators.note: empty of its inside, so the outer letters of Kirk

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sci-fi fan races after an empty-headed Captain Kirk into the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Star Trek, the series featuring Captain Kirk, a kind of science-fiction fan.

clue.text: Dumped unceremoniously in seat, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the word is said aloud and heard as another

parts.note: a throne is a royal seat

explanation.surface: A monarch tipped off the seat, as it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurled or tossed, as of something cast down without care.
